newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea set to help banks' overseas activities.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea set to help banks' overseas activities.

text.p: South Korean finance minister Kang Kyong-shik said on Monday the government would support overseas activities of financial institutions with its foreign currency reserves if necessary.
"If needed, (the government) plans to aid business activities of our financial institutions in international markets through foreign currency reserves," Kang told Kia Group creditors at a luncheon.
Fears of difficulty in raising funds from abroad have haunted South Korean banks following a string of corporate collapses earlier this year.

Two leading international credit-rating agencies have announced they were reviewing several big South Korean banks for possible downgrading because of the continued deterioration of their asset quality.
Kia Group, the latest victim, was put under the protection of its creditor banks on July 15 after they determined Kia would default on debt payments.
Kang has said repeatedly that the government would not intervene to help Kia.
